evidence.field: 學 formation paragraph; exact occurrences: the graph after 冖 and before 亦声; the parenthetical after 两臼或省作; comparison with the earlier jù-labeled graph and the 两臼 in 两臼.
evidence.text: The passage reads as an analysis from 两臼, followed by a parenthetical visibly resembling “犹廾,” then 从冖 plus a printed graph before 亦声; it then says 两臼或省作 followed by another printed graph. Thus the source explicitly names two 臼 and appears to compare their configuration to 廾: grammatically, it presents two 臼 shapes as a grouped configuration, rather than naming a two-hands/two-claws unit in place of 臼. The phrase assigns 亦声 to the graph immediately after 冖, not to the entire combination. In my visual comparison, the graph after 冖 has a compact, paired-stroke appearance resembling the earlier graph labeled jù; the graph after 省作 is a separate, more abbreviated-looking form. The ordinary printed 臼 tokens in 两臼 are visually identifiable as 臼. These visual observations do not establish exact Unicode identities for the rare graphs or the small parenthetical graph.
